Developers.metaDescription: Submit content for verification and read Zuula fact-checks from your own newsroom tools.

banner.title: Zuula API
banner.description: Submit content for verification and read fact-checks from your own newsroom tools.

preview.title: Preview, subject to change until v1
preview.body: This is an early look at the API for journalists and partners. It is not callable yet: the backend ships in Phase 2, and endpoints, fields and limits may change before version 1.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: The Zuula API gives accredited journalists and partner organisations the same verification that powers zuula.ug. Checks run asynchronously:
overview.step1: Send content to POST /v1/checks. You get a tracking ID straight away.
overview.step2: Poll GET /v1/checks/[trackingId] until the status is completed.
overview.step3: Read the verdict, confidence score, explanation and citations from the result.
overview.format: JSON over HTTPS (UTF-8). Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.body: Every request needs an API key in the Authorization header. Verified journalists and administrators can create and revoke keys in Account → API access. Keys start with zl_live_ and are shown only once.

scopes.submit: Send text, links, articles and media for checking.
scopes.read: Read check results and search published fact-checks.

auth.serverOnly: Never put an API key in a web page, mobile app or public repository. Call the API from your own server and revoke any key that may have leaked.

rate.title: Rate limits
rate.body: Each key can make {limit} requests per hour. Every response reports your remaining allowance. When you go over it, the API answers 429 Too Many Requests: wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After before trying again.

headers.limit: Requests allowed per hour for this key.
headers.remaining: Requests left in the current hour.
headers.reset: When the allowance resets, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.
headers.retryAfter: Sent with 429 responses: seconds to wait before retrying.

submit.title: Submit a check
submit.body: Send one item for verification. Use JSON for text, links and articles, and multipart/form-data for media files. The response arrives immediately with a tracking ID; the check itself takes about 10 seconds for text and up to a minute for media.

fields.content: The text to check. Up to {textMax} characters for text, {articleMax} for an article. Required for text and article.
fields.url: A full http or https link to a news article or web page. Required for url.
fields.file: The photo, voice note or video, up to {size}. JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, AAC, MP4, MOV, WebM or 3GP. Required for media.
fields.headline: Optional article headline, up to {max} characters.
fields.language: Language of the content: en, lg, ach, nyn, teo, or auto to detect it (the default).

status.title: Get a result
status.body: Returns the state of a check. When the status is completed, the result field holds the full fact-check object. Tracking IDs look like ZL-7K3P-Q9.

states.queued: Received and waiting to be analysed.
states.processing: Claims are being cross-checked against trusted sources and AI-detection models.
states.failed: The check could not be completed. The error field explains why.

search.title: Search fact-checks
search.body: Search the public library of completed fact-checks. Results are ranked by Community Confidence Score and recency, and verdicts suspended for review are left out.

params.q: Words to look for in titles, summaries and checked text.
params.category: Filter by topic, such as Health or Elections.
params.language: Filter by the language of the checked content.
params.dates: Only checks made on or after, and on or before, these dates (YYYY-MM-DD).
params.perPage: Results per page, from 1 to 50. Default 20.

factCheck.title: Fact-check object
factCheck.body: Completed checks and search results share this shape. Arrays may be empty; fields may be added before v1 but not removed.

fields.id: Permanent ID of the published fact-check.
fields.trackingId: The tracking ID returned when the content was submitted.
fields.confidence: How confident Zuula is in the verdict, from 0 to 100.
fields.summary: A plain-language explanation of the verdict.
fields.findings: Short statements of what is false and what is actually true.
fields.claims: Claims found in the text, with character offsets, an assessment, the reason and the citations that back it.
fields.citations: Sources used, with name, title, link, publication date and stance: supports, contradicts or context.
fields.aiSignals: Checks for AI-generated or manipulated content, each with a score, the threshold and the method.
fields.community: Accurate and inaccurate rating counts from the public, journalists and experts.
fields.humanReview: Present when an expert confirmed or overrode the verdict, with their justification.

errors.title: Errors
errors.body: Errors use standard HTTP status codes and a JSON body with a machine-readable code and a human-readable message.

codes.bad_request: The request is malformed or a required field is missing.
codes.unauthorized: The API key is missing, invalid or revoked.
codes.forbidden: The key does not have the scope this endpoint needs.
codes.not_found: No check or fact-check has that ID.
codes.file_too_large: The media file is larger than 50 MB.
codes.unsupported_media: The file type is not accepted.
codes.invalid_content: The content is too short, too long or not a valid link.
codes.rate_limited: The key has used its hourly allowance. Wait for Retry-After seconds.
codes.server_error: Something went wrong on our side. Try again later.

report.title: Get a fact-check
report.body: Returns one published fact-check by its ID: the same data behind the public <link>report page</link>, including the verdict, confidence, explanation, citations and community ratings.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.body: Planned alongside the API so you don't have to poll: a callback to your server when a check's verdict is ready. This section will be filled in once webhook delivery is designed in Phase 2. The Zuula bots on <link>WhatsApp and Telegram</link> are being built on the same infrastructure.

access.title: Get access
access.body: Verified journalists and administrators can create a key today in <keys>Account → API access</keys>; it will start working when the API goes live in Phase 2. For a newsroom integration or a higher rate limit, email <email>hello@zuula.ug</email>. Using the API means accepting the <terms>API terms</terms>.

languages.body: English, Luganda, Acholi, Runyankole and Ateso.

mission.title: Uganda sees a flood of forwarded claims every day. Zuula checks them before you share.
mission.body: Zuula (branded from Uganda Fact-Guard) is an AI-assisted fact-checking platform built for how news actually travels here — on WhatsApp, in group chats and on social media, often faster than any newsroom can verify it. Submit a claim and get a verdict backed by evidence, not just an opinion.

methodology.title: How we reach a verdict
methodology.description: Every check follows the same four steps, whether it's automated or escalated to a human reviewer.

submit.title: You submit a claim
submit.body: Paste text, share a link or upload media (up to 50 MB). You get a tracking ID and can follow the analysis live.

check.title: We check it
check.body: The claim is cross-referenced against trusted Ugandan and international sources, and screened for AI-generated text, deepfakes and manipulated audio or video.

publish.title: A verdict is published
publish.body: You see the verdict, the evidence behind it and which sources agree or disagree — never just a label.

review.title: The community and our reviewers weigh in
review.body: Readers rate the verdict. If enough people disagree, an accredited Expert reviews the case and can confirm or override it — the report is then marked “Human Verified.”

independence.title: Rules we hold ourselves to
independence.description: Zuula's verdicts aren't for sale, and they aren't final without a way to challenge them.

label.title: We label, we don't delete
label.body: Zuula never removes anyone's post. We publish an independent verdict and evidence alongside it.

rules.title: Every rating carries the same rules
rules.body: Public, Journalist and Expert ratings feed the same Community Confidence Score, just weighted by track record — nobody's vote is discounted without a reason.

accountable.title: Reviewers are accountable
accountable.body: Expert overrides require a written justification and are recorded in an append-only audit log that Admins can inspect.

sources.title: Sources are shown, not hidden
sources.body: Every report links the evidence it was checked against, so you can verify our reasoning yourself.

whatsapp.title: Check a claim from WhatsApp
whatsapp.description: No app, no data bundle for a browser — forward the message and get a verdict back in the chat.
whatsapp.body: A WhatsApp and Telegram bot is planned for the platform's API phase, so you'll be able to forward a message straight to Zuula the way you already forward it to friends. It isn't live yet — for now, use <link>Verify</link> on the web.

free.a: Checking a claim and reading the Library is free for everyone. Journalist and Expert accounts need accreditation, since they carry more weight in the community score and can review flagged cases.

submit.a: Text (like a WhatsApp forward), a link, a full article, or media — photos, voice notes and video up to 50 MB.

time.q: How long does a check take?
time.a: Text usually takes about 10 seconds. Media can take up to a minute. Cases escalated to an Expert reviewer follow a review deadline instead.

disagree.q: What if I disagree with a verdict?
disagree.a: Rate it. Ratings from the Public, Journalists and Experts are combined into a Community Confidence Score. If a verdict's score drops low enough with enough ratings, it's flagged for an Expert to review and confirm or override.

languages.a: Claims can be checked in English, Luganda, Acholi, Runyankole and Ateso. The interface is being translated into those languages too; anything not yet translated appears in English.

data.a: Under Uganda's Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019. See our <link>Privacy Policy</link>.

who.a: Zuula (“Uganda Fact-Guard”) is developed by the Centre for Intelligent Technologies at Victoria University Kampala as an academic and public-interest project. Verdicts are reached independently of any funder or advertiser.

contact.title: Get in touch
contact.description: Questions about a verdict, the platform or a partnership.

privacy.metaDescription: How Zuula collects, uses and protects your data.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: How we collect, use and protect your data.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: This policy explains what Zuula collects when you check a claim, browse the Library or create an account, and how that information is used and protected under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019 of Uganda. It applies to the Zuula website and, once launched, the WhatsApp and Telegram bots and partner API.

items.account: Account details — name, email or phone number, and role (Public, Journalist, Expert or Admin).
items.submissions: Submissions — the text, link or media you ask Zuula to check, and the tracking ID it's given.
items.ratings: Ratings and reports — the verdicts you rate, comments you leave, and content you flag for moderation.
items.accreditation: Accreditation documents — for Journalist and Expert applications, the credentials you provide for review.
items.device: Device and usage information — pages visited, browser type and rough location, to keep the service secure and working.

items.pipeline: To run the claim through our detection pipeline and show you its status and verdict.
items.ccs: To weight and combine community ratings into a Community Confidence Score.
items.accreditation: To review Journalist and Expert accreditation, and to record reviewer decisions in an audit log.
items.abuse: To detect coordinated or manipulated rating activity and protect the platform from abuse.
items.accuracy: To measure and improve verdict accuracy over time.

aiSharing.title: AI analysis and third parties
aiSharing.body: Checking a claim can involve sending its text, or a transcription of its audio or video, to automated detection models and, for evidence retrieval, to a hosted AI provider. Media you upload is scanned for malware before it's processed.
aiSharing.review: Because some of these providers may process data outside Uganda, we are reviewing this data flow against the Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019 before it is enabled outside the current mock-data build. This section will be updated once that review is complete.

dppa.title: Your rights under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019
dppa.intro: As a data subject under Ugandan law, you have the right to:

items.access: Access the personal data we hold about you.
items.delete: Request deletion of your account data, subject to our retention obligations below.
items.object: Object to, or ask us to restrict, certain processing.
items.complain: Lodge a complaint with Uganda's Personal Data Protection Office (National Information Technology Authority-Uganda) if you believe we've mishandled your data.

dppa.outro: To exercise any of these rights, contact us using the details in <contact>Contact & data requests</contact> below.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.body: Published verdicts and their evidence form part of the public fact-check record and are kept indefinitely, in the same way a news archive is. Account details are kept while your account is active and for a limited period afterwards, to support audit and accreditation records required for the review process. Malware-scanned upload copies are retained only as long as needed to produce a verdict.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.body: We use a session cookie to keep you signed in, and local storage to remember your theme and language preference on this device. We don't use third-party advertising trackers.

children.title: Children's privacy
children.body: Zuula is intended for users aged 18 and over. We don't knowingly collect personal data from children, and will delete any we become aware of.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: We'll update the date at the top of this page whenever this policy changes, and post material changes on the <home>homepage</home> before they take effect.

contact.title: Contact & data requests
contact.body: Email <email>privacy@zuula.ug</email> for any question about this policy or to exercise your rights under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019. See also our <terms>Terms of use</terms>.

terms.metaDescription: The terms that govern using Zuula.
terms.title: Terms
terms.description: The terms that govern using Zuula.

acceptance.title: Acceptance of these terms
acceptance.body: By using Zuula — the website, and in future the WhatsApp/Telegram bots and partner API — you agree to these terms. If you don't agree, please don't use the service.

service.title: What Zuula is (and isn't)
service.body: Zuula checks claims, links and media using automated detection and, where a case is escalated, human review by accredited reviewers. A verdict reflects our best assessment of the evidence available when it was published, and can change if better evidence emerges. Zuula is a fact-checking tool, not legal, medical or financial advice, and a verdict is not a substitute for your own judgement.

items.roles: Anyone can sign up as a Public user. Journalist and Expert roles require accreditation.
items.accurate: Give accurate information when you sign up or apply for accreditation.
items.one: Keep one account per person, and keep your credentials confidential — you're responsible for activity under your account.
items.twoFactor: Two-factor authentication is required for Expert and Admin accounts.

submissions.title: Your submissions
submissions.body: You must have the right to share whatever you submit for checking. Don't submit content that's illegal, that violates someone else's privacy, or that you don't have permission to share.
submissions.publish: Uploaded files are scanned for malware before analysis. A submission and the verdict Zuula reaches on it may be published as part of the public fact-check record, in the same way a newsroom publishes what it fact-checks.

ratings.title: Community ratings and conduct
ratings.body: Rate verdicts honestly, based on the evidence shown. Coordinated or manipulated rating activity (for example, groups of accounts rating together to push a verdict's score) can have its ratings discounted and the accounts involved suspended. You can report content or ratings that look manipulated from the report page.

api.title: API and developer access
api.body: Journalist and Admin accounts can request API keys from <keys>Account → API Keys</keys>. Partner API access is rate limited (currently {limit} requests/hour) and keys are tied to your account — don't share them. See the <dev>developer page</dev> for details.

ip.title: Intellectual property
ip.body: The Zuula name, mark and interface belong to the Centre for Intelligent Technologies, Victoria University Kampala. You're welcome to share, screenshot and cite Zuula's published verdicts with attribution and a link back to the report.

disclaimer.title: Accuracy and limitation of liability
disclaimer.body: We check every claim in good faith and publish the evidence behind each verdict, but we don't guarantee any verdict is error-free. To the extent permitted by the laws of Uganda, Zuula and Victoria University CIT aren't liable for decisions made in reliance on a verdict.

termination.title: Suspension and termination
termination.body: We may suspend or close an account for abuse, manipulated ratings, or breaking these terms. You can close your own account at any time from Account settings.

law.title: Governing law
law.body: These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Uganda.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.body: We may update these terms as the platform develops. We'll update the date above when we do; continuing to use Zuula after a change means you accept the updated terms.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Questions about these terms? Email <email>hello@zuula.ug</email>. See also our <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy>.
